query: Which material can be used for superconducting properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A refractory high‐entropy alloy with equiatomic composition (specifically W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20) can exhibit superconducting behavior at sufficiently low temperatures due to the presence of known superconducting elements such as Nb and Ta embedded in a chemically disordered, single‐phase BCC matrix that supports electron–phonon coupling required for Cooper pairing.
generation.material_initial_state: A cast or additively manufactured (e.g., via PBF-LB/M) refractory high‐entropy alloy with nominal composition W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 and a homogeneous BCC structure.
generation.intervention: Cooling the material to cryogenic temperatures (e.g., below 10 K) under controlled laboratory conditions.
generation.conditions: Measurements performed in a cryogenic environment with minimal external magnetic fields and stable thermal conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: The single-phase, chemically disordered BCC structure that incorporates superconducting elements (Nb, Ta) while maintaining high mixing entropy, which may preserve favorable electron–phonon interactions.
generation.mechanism: Electron–phonon coupling in the disordered alloy facilitates Cooper pair formation. Despite the scattering inherent to high-entropy systems, conventional s-wave superconductivity may persist due to the robustness of the pairing mechanism (Anderson theorem effect) in such materials.
generation.predicted_outcome: A sharp drop in electrical resistance (approaching zero) at a well-defined critical temperature, accompanied by signatures in magnetic susceptibility (such as the Meissner effect) that confirm the onset of superconductivity.
generation.baseline: At room temperature and intermediate temperatures, the alloy exhibits conventional metallic (non-superconducting) behavior with finite resistance.
generation.boundary: Superconductivity, if present, will only manifest below a specific low-temperature threshold (likely below ~10 K) and may be sensitive to slight compositional variations or external magnetic fields, which can suppress the superconducting state.
generation.uncertainty: The exact critical temperature and the magnitude of the superconducting energy gap in this high-entropy alloy are uncertain due to the complex interplay of chemical disorder and electron scattering; furthermore, disorder effects might both enhance and weaken superconductivity depending on the detailed microstructure.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate samples of the W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 alloy using established casting or additive manufacturing methods. Then, using a four-probe electrical measurement setup integrated within a cryogenic system, gradually lower the temperature while continuously recording the electrical resistance. Complement this with magnetic susceptibility and heat capacity measurements to detect the superconducting transition.
measurements: Electrical resistance as a function of temperature
Magnetic susceptibility (to detect the Meissner effect)
Heat capacity near the expected transition temperature
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no clear and abrupt transition to near-zero electrical resistance is observed below a distinct critical temperature (e.g., below ~10 K), and if complementary measurements (magnetic susceptibility and heat capacity) do not indicate superconducting behavior, then the hypothesis that W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 exhibits superconductivity is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Though there are more recent refractory metal high entropy alloys with superior properties reported in the literature [ [7] ], the alloy W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 was selected for this work’s experiments. Since the concept of refractory metal high entropy alloys is comparably young, and the number of possible alloy combinations is vast, there are only single publications on most of the different alloy combinations, thus providing only limited information per alloy. W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 is one of the first refractory metal high entropy alloys developed by Senkov et al. [ [18] ] and therefore also one of the best investigated ones. Consequently there are at least a few publications available that allow a comparison with the results and support discussion.

For the experiments, a heterogeneous mixture of five single element powders was used to prepare the WMoTaNbV samples. The specifications of the powders used for the PBF-LB/M experiments were chosen based on literature and our own experience.
